050.benefits: Service members and their families get pay, housing, and health care. Defense companies, and the workers and towns that build equipment or host military bases, receive much of the rest.

150.plain: U.S. embassies and diplomats, foreign aid for health, food, development, and disaster relief, military aid to partner countries, and dues to international groups such as the United Nations. It also pays for passport and visa services. In 2025, most programs of the U.S. Agency for International Development moved to the State Department.
150.benefits: Americans who travel or live abroad get passports and help from U.S. embassies and consulates. People in developing countries receive health, food, and disaster aid, and partner militaries receive U.S. equipment and training.

270.plain: Energy Department research on energy technologies, efficiency and weatherization grants, the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. It also includes the Tennessee Valley Authority, a federally owned power company that pays its own way through electricity sales.
270.benefits: Households and businesses benefit from an emergency oil supply that can steady fuel markets during disruptions. Low-income families get help sealing and insulating their homes, and about 10 million people in seven Southeastern states get electricity from TVA through local utilities.

370.plain: Federal Housing Administration mortgage insurance, deposit insurance that protects bank accounts, Small Business Administration loans, and the Postal Service. It also funds the Census Bureau and agencies that support business, such as the patent office and the National Institute of Standards and Technology. In FY2026 this category took in more than it spent, mainly because the FDIC's deposit insurance fund and FHA's mortgage insurance fund collected more in premiums and other income than they paid out.
370.benefits: Home buyers with FHA-insured mortgages, many of them first-time buyers, and small business owners with SBA-backed loans. Anyone with money in an FDIC-insured bank is protected up to $250,000 per depositor, per bank, for each account ownership category.

States, cities, and counties use block grants for local projects, with most of the money required to benefit low- and moderate-income residents, and rural communities get loans and grants for water, housing, and businesses.

900.plain: Interest the government pays to people and institutions that lend it money by buying Treasury securities, minus interest it earns on its own loans and cash. Interest paid to Social Security and other federal trust funds is left out because it is a payment from one part of the government to another.
900.benefits: The interest goes to whoever holds Treasury debt. More than half is held by U.S. investors such as pension funds, banks, mutual funds, insurance companies, state and local governments, and individuals. The Federal Reserve holds about 1 in 7 dollars of this debt, and foreign investors and governments hold roughly 3 in 10.
